q1_issues.issue: (Member northcove summer_cadence) asserts the Northcove IS a summer cadence: the change-of-kind State-result shape ('turned into a museum') was applied to 'returned to its summer cadence', where the subject resumes operating AT a cadence rather than becoming one, so the flat dual-emit half (and the (Experiencer sk_cadence_1 northcove) at 41) states the wrong fact.

The possessive 'its' in 'its summer cadence' is dropped - no (Possession sk_cadence_1 northcove), although the parallel 'its distillation' at statement 47 does carry its possessor through the event-noun subject-role rule.

'the NEXT full-moon meeting' loses 'next' entirely: no ordering atom relates the meeting to the equinox, while the parse does emit (Before sk_close_1 sk_stepdown_1) for 'the following two weeks', so the same qualifier is carried in one place and silently dropped in the other.

(Patient sk_come_1 sk_equinox_1) makes the equinox a change-of-state undergoer; an arriving equinox neither changes nor self-propels, so the intransitive-subject tests give Theme (or Agent as the stated fallback), and the light-verb-over-event-noun rule would put the date atoms on sk_equinox_1 with no separate come event.

q2_gaps: a time-denoting definite NP as clause subject coreferring with a stated date ('On day 555 ... The day was clear and warm') - Time atoms are specified to attach to an event witness or event-denoting noun, so (Time sk_day_1 (Day 555)) on a day entity is outside the stated attachment rule, and there is no identity relation to use instead
'during / for the following two weeks' - a bare temporal-interval NP: During requires an eventuality as its outer argument, and no encoding refers to an interval span itself
'the next N' where N is an event-noun rather than a calendar unit ('the next full-moon meeting') - the next/following term-propagation rule covers morning / day / week / month / year only

'returned to its X' (resumption of a prior operating mode) - neither the motion-result Goal route nor the change-of-kind State-result route fits a mode/cadence NP, and nothing licenses a 'back to a prior state' reading
a day-of-year date in a non-Gregorian calendar ('day 555 of Year 2') - the (Day n) term takes the integer, but the seeded calendar-ordering machinery assumes day-of-month numbering
notes: Strong elsewhere: the phrasal verb step_down kept whole, the definite-group per-member distribution rule, the 'its distillation' possessor as the event-noun's Agent, and the nominalization's (Of sk_collection_1 silken_thread) with the material-adjective modifier genus are all exactly as the instruction set specifies.
